papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Gastric signet ring cell carcinoma (SRCC) typically metastasizes to the liver and peritoneum. Although pulmonary metastasis occurs in approximately 15% of patients with advanced gastric cancer and typically presents as multiple well-circumscribed nodules on chest computed tomography (CT), diffuse ground-glass opacities (GGOs) as the predominant manifestation of SRCC lung metastasis are exceedingly rare. This pattern may pose a diagnostic pitfall by closely mimicking infectious or interstitial lung diseases. CASE DESCRIPTION: We report two cases of gastric SRCC with pulmonary metastasis presenting primarily with respiratory symptoms and atypical imaging features. Case 1: A 64-year-old woman presented with persistent cough, dyspnea, and chest pain, and denied any preceding gastrointestinal symptoms. Chest CT revealed bilateral diffuse GGOs accompanied by pleural effusion and thickening. Despite empirical antibiotic therapy directed against Streptococcus pyogenes and Klebsiella pneumoniae identified by next-generation sequencing, her symptoms worsened. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) demonstrated intense metabolic activity [maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) 6.2] in the lung lesions and bilateral pleural involvement. Bronchoscopy-guided biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma with signet ring cell features, and gastroscopy with biopsy of a depressed gastric angle lesion confirmed poorly differentiated gastric adenocarcinoma. She received docetaxel plus oxaliplatin chemotherapy with symptomatic improvement and was discharged. Case 2: A 62-year-old woman presented with exertional dyspnea and intermittent cough, also without preceding gastrointestinal symptoms. CT imaging demonstrated right pleural effusion, pleural thickening, and ground-glass nodules. Empirical antibiotic therapy was ineffective. Pleural fluid analysis revealed elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA; 85.00 µg/mL) and cancer antigen 125 (CA125; 327.00 U/mL). Biopsy of an adnexal mass and gastric lesions confirmed gastric SRCC with pleural and ovarian metastases. She was referred to the oncology department for systemic therapy. Long-term follow-up data for both patients are not available in the medical records. CONCLUSIONS: These cases highlight an atypical imaging pattern of gastric SRCC metastasis-diffuse GGOs with pleural involvement-that closely mimics benign lung diseases. In patients without known malignancy who present with unexplained respiratory symptoms, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusion or thickening, and poor response to anti-infective therapy, early lung or pleural biopsy is essential to prevent diagnostic delay and initiate timely systemic oncological treatment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastasis remains an important clinical concern in patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC), even after prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI). Accurate identification of patients at high risk of brain metastasis after PCI may facilitate individualized surveillance and management. This study developed a fusion model based on two-and-a-half-dimensional (2.5D) multi-channel deep learning features, clinical features, and radiomics features to predict whether patients with SCLC will develop brain metastases following PCI. METHODS: This retrospective study included 185 patients with SCLC who underwent PCI and randomly divided them into a training set (N=148) and a testing set (N=37). A 2.5D multi-channel convolutional neural network (CNN) model was constructed based on multi-planar regions of interest (ROI) derived from CT images to extract 2.5D deep learning features. Based on the largest cross-section and three-dimensional (3D) volume of the tumor ROI, two-dimensional (2D) and 3D deep learning features were extracted, respectively. Subsequently, features from different dimensions were fused with clinical features and traditional omics features to construct the 2D_clinic_Rad, 2.5D_clinic_Rad, and 3D_clinic_Rad models, respectively. The performance differences between the 3D models and the clinical and traditional radiomics models were then compared. RESULTS: The 2.5D_clinic_Rad fusion model demonstrated the best performance in predicting brain metastases, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.841 on the test set, outperforming clinical models, traditional radiomics models, and 2D and 3D deep learning fusion models. Analysis of decision curves and calibration curves indicated that the 2.5D_clinic_Rad model demonstrated the highest clinical net benefit and the best calibration consistency compared to other models. CONCLUSIONS: The fusion model based on 2.5D_clinic_Rad can effectively predict the risk of brain metastasis in patients with SCLC following whole-brain prophylactic irradiation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved rapidly from a surgery-centered approach toward biomarker-informed, multimodality care integrating staging, pathology, surgery, perioperative systemic treatment, and postoperative surveillance. In Vietnam, implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions, particularly in access to fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), invasive mediastinal staging, molecular testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. This project aimed to develop a Vietnamese multidisciplinary expert consensus to contextualize contemporary international evidence for clinical practice in Vietnam. METHODS: A structured, modified Delphi-informed consensus process was conducted in Vietnam between August 2025 and January 2026. The workflow comprised seven stages: scoping; a baseline practice survey; initial draft development; expert review of parts 1 and 2; post-meeting written feedback, revision, electronic recirculation, and formal voting for these sections; a multidisciplinary consensus meeting and formal voting for parts 3 and 4; and editorial harmonization and consolidation. The panel included specialists in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, respiratory medicine, pathology, nuclear medicine, radiation oncology, and related disciplines. Classes of recommendation were adapted from the European Society of Cardiology framework. All statements submitted to formal consensus voting were formally rated, with consensus predefined as at least 75% agreement. RESULTS: The final document comprised 35 consensus statements across four domains: preoperative diagnosis and staging (n=7), surgery and postoperative surveillance (n=8), neoadjuvant and perioperative treatment (n=12), and adjuvant treatment (n=8). Across the meeting rosters, 32 unique experts were identified, with strong representation from thoracic surgery and medical oncology. The baseline survey and expert discussions highlighted implementation gaps in FDG-PET/CT, invasive mediastinal staging, biomarker testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. All 35 consensus statements met the predefined threshold, with agreement ranging from 82% to 100%. CONCLUSIONS: These consensus statements provide a multidisciplinary, evidence-informed framework for the diagnosis and management of resectable NSCLC across the perioperative pathway. By contextualizing international evidence within Vietnamese clinical practice, the document may help improve consistency of care, support biomarker-guided and multimodality treatment, and strengthen multidisciplinary decision-making across institutions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab is a standard first-line treatment for advanced or recurrent non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable driver alterations, including tumors with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor proportion score (TPS) <50%. However, the clinical benefits vary, and biomarkers for this chemoimmunotherapy regimen remain limited. CBM588, a live biotherapeutic preparation containing Clostridium butyricum MIYAIRI, may modulate antitumor immunity by affecting the gut microbiota. The MIYABRO study aims to evaluate the additive efficacy and safety of CBM588 with platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab and to explore longitudinal gut microbiota dynamics. METHODS: This is a multi-institutional, single-arm, phase II exploratory study enrolling 20 treatment-naïve patients with advanced or recurrent non-squamous NSCLC and a PD-L1 TPS <50%. Patients will receive continuous CBM588 from the start of the protocol treatment in combination with platinum, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab. After four induction cycles, maintenance pemetrexed plus pembrolizumab will be continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoints are response rate and progression-free survival (PFS). Tumor response will be assessed according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Stool samples will be collected before treatment, cycle 3, and cycle 5 for 16S rRNA sequencing to evaluate microbial diversity and responder-associated taxa. DISCUSSION: This trial will prospectively assess CBM588 added to platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab in NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS <50% while monitoring the gut microbiota. These findings may inform microbiota-targeted strategies for optimizing chemoimmunotherapy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (No. jRCT1071260004) on 6 April 2026.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a third-generation, irreversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), nevertheless, the inevitable occurrence of osimertinib resistance after a long-term administration limits its clinical application in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Xanthatin, a naturally active component from Xanthium Strumarium L., has been shown to possess multiple bioactive effects. However, whether xanthatin can ameliorate osimertinib resistance remains unclear. PURPOSE: The present study aimed to clarify the role and detailed mechanism of xanthatin in reversing osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. METHODS: Combenefit analysis, LDH release assay, and EdU staining were employed to evaluate the effect of xanthatin on osimertinib cytotoxicity in osimertinib-resistant (OR) NSCLC cells. Quantitative proteomics combined with bioinformatics and network pharmacology analysis was used to uncover the specific target of xanthatin. Xanthatin-triggered HMGCR protein degradation was assessed by bio-layer interferometry, drug affinity responsive target stability assay, cycloheximide chase assay and ubiquitination determination. The function of xanthatin on cholesterol homeostasis was measured via the detection of HMGCR activity, total cholesterol, triglycerides and lipid droplets as well as MDR1 distribution in the lipid rafts. The function of MDR1 was examined via a rhodamine 123 efflux assay. The accumulation and efflux of osimertinib were monitored using FITC-labeled osimertinib. The effect of HMGCR on the cytotoxicity of xanthatin was evaluated through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments in HMGCR-overexpressing NSCLC OR cells. RESULTS: Xanthatin restored the sensitivity of NSCLC OR cells to osimertinib, accompanied by the induction of oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Proteomic data indicate that oxidative stress and metabolic reprogramming contribute to xanthatin-induced apoptosis in NSCLC OR cells. Through further integration with network pharmacology, we identified HMGCR (a key enzyme of cholesterol metabolism) as a potential target of xanthatin. We confirmed xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR protein (KD=6.753 μM), subsequently facilitating AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGCR. Xanthatin diminished intracellular cholesterol biosynthesis and MDR1 levels in lipid rafts. HMGCR overexpression mitigated the cytotoxicity of xanthatin and sustained cholesterol homeostasis, enabling tolerance to the combined effects of xanthatin and osimertinib. Conversely, HMGCR-deficient NSCLC OR cells were more vulnerable to osimertinib. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates for the first time that xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR and promotes AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination of HMGCR, which in turn accelerates HMGCR degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, leading to reduced cholesterol synthesis, less distribution of MDR1 in lipid rafts, ROS accumulation, and mitochondrial dysfunction-associated apoptosis, ultimately restoring osimertinib sensitivity in NSCLC cells. Therefore, xanthatin may represent a preclinical natural product candidate for the reversal of osimertinib resistance in NSCLC cells, which requires further translational verification in future studies.

papers.abstract_en: Low-dose computed tomography screening has markedly increased the detection of small, deeply located subsolid pulmonary nodules, and local therapy for these lesions now encompasses anatomical segmentectomy, tailored sublobar resection, lobectomy, and image-guided thermal ablation. The framework does not expand indications beyond those already supported by guidelines. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection for improving patient survival. Current imaging‑based methods for pulmonary nodule (PN) detection are often limited by low efficiency and suboptimal accuracy, falling short of the demands for precise clinical diagnosis. The baseline YOLOv8 model, although efficient, is prone to missed detections due to non-maximum suppression (NMS)‑induced suppression of small nodules and insufficient feature extraction for morphologically complex lesions. To address these clinical challenges, this study aimed to optimize YOLOv8 by integrating a real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) decoder head and an aggregated attention mechanism, thereby improving detection sensitivity and accuracy for PNs of varying sizes and shapes. METHODS: The proposed model, termed YOLOv8‑RTA, integrates an RT‑DETR‑based transformer decoder head into YOLOv8, replacing the original detection head to mitigate NMS‑induced suppression of true boxes, and introduces an aggregated attention mechanism within the backbone to expand the effective receptive field and enhance deep feature discriminability. Training and evaluation were performed on the Tianchi dataset, with five‑fold cross‑validation and an external test on 50 hospital Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) computed tomography (CT) scans. RESULTS: YOLOv8‑RTA achieved precision of 93.28%, recall of 92.4%, and mean average precision at 50% intersection over union (mAP50) of 94.98% on the Tianchi dataset. Compared to the baseline YOLOv8 model, which achieved an mAP50 of 90.6%, the proposed method improved the detection accuracy by 4.38 percentage points. It also outperformed RT‑DETR‑R18, which attained an mAP50 of 93.51%, by a margin of 1.47 percentage points. The model contains only 6.24 million parameters and runs at 12.2 giga floating point operations per second (GFLOPs). In five‑fold cross‑validation, the mAP50 ranged from 75.4% to 99.3%, with a mean value of 91.5%. On the external PACS dataset, the model detected all 50 nodules, achieving a mean confidence score of 0.86 for nodules smaller than 5 mm. CONCLUSIONS: This study proposes YOLOv8‑RTA, a collaborative hybrid network that combines an RT‑DETR decoder head and an aggregated attention module to enhance multi‑scale feature extraction and discriminative representation for PN detection. On the Tianchi dataset, the model achieved improved performance over baseline YOLOv8 and RT‑DETR‑R18, with gains of 4.38 and 1.47 percentage points in mAP50, respectively, while maintaining a lightweight architecture of only 6.24 million parameters. A preliminary test on 50 real‑world PACS CT images suggests potential clinical feasibility, with all nodules successfully detected in this limited cohort. These findings indicate that YOLOv8‑RTA offers a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade‑off for PN screening. Future work will focus on larger multi‑center validation, patient‑level cross‑validation, and extension to three-dimensional (3D) context modelling.

papers.abstract_en: Minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS) has evolved significantly over the past two decades, shifting from conventional median sternotomy toward sternal-sparing approaches that offer reduced surgical trauma, lower complication rates, and faster patient recovery. As incision size has progressively decreased, the field has advanced toward totally endoscopic cardiac surgery (TECS), in which the entire intracardiac procedure is performed exclusively under thoracoscopic visualization. Drawing on our institutional experience at Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, and a review of the current literature, we provide a comprehensive overview of the key elements required to successfully build and sustain a TECS program. Both non-robotic and robotic-assisted endoscopic platforms are discussed. Large-scale evidence confirms that MICS and TECS achieve outcomes equivalent or superior to sternotomy, with low mortality and stroke rates, and significantly improved health-related quality of life. Notably, non-robotic TECS offers a scalable and cost-effective pathway that does not require an expert bedside assistant, can address multiple pathologies simultaneously, and is feasible across diverse healthcare settings. Emerging technologies-including articulated robotic instruments, artificial intelligence-enhanced imaging, and next-generation robotic platforms-are expected to further expand the reach and safety of fully endoscopic cardiac procedures.

papers.abstract_en: Thoracic surgery has progressively moved from open thoracotomy to video-assisted and robot-assisted approaches, reducing access-related trauma while changing the technical environment in which pulmonary resections are performed and taught. This narrative review examines the clinical evolution of open, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS), with particular attention to the evidence supporting their perioperative and oncological outcomes, the learning curves associated with minimally invasive surgery, and the role of simulation-based training. Randomized trials now provide robust evidence that VATS improve postoperative recovery compared with thoracotomy in appropriately selected patients with predominantly early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, without compromising long-term oncological outcomes. Randomized comparisons between RATS and VATS support RATS as an oncologically acceptable minimally invasive alternative and suggest advantages in selected technical endpoints, particularly blood loss and lymph node retrieval, but do not demonstrate consistent superiority in major clinical or survival outcomes. Learning curves vary according to previous experience, case complexity, supervision, institutional volume, and the endpoint used to define competence, making fixed case-number thresholds an incomplete measure of proficiency. Simulation can improve selected technical skills and provide objective performance assessment, although evidence becomes progressively less robust when moving from simulator performance to operating room transfer and patient-level outcomes. Surgical approach, therefore, should be interpreted within a broader framework that includes patient and tumour characteristics, oncological quality, surgical expertise, institutional resources, and structured training.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Surgical access and one-lung ventilation (OLV) may generate distinct systemic and local inflammatory responses after lung resection. We compared perioperative cytokine profiles in serum, pleural fluid, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open thoracotomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: This prospective, single-center, non-randomized observational study included 40 adults undergoing anatomical lobectomy with mediastinal lymph-node dissection (VATS, n = 20; open thoracotomy, n = 20). Surgical access was selected according to patient preference. TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10 were measured in serial serum and pleural-fluid samples and in BAL from both lungs before OLV and after resection. Results: Serum and pleural-fluid cytokines peaked at 4 h in both groups. Exploratory pointwise comparisons showed that at 24 h, serum TNF-α (4.89 [IQR, 4.43-5.92] vs. 4.01 [IQR, 3.75-5.12] pg/mL; p = 0.010), IL-6 (150.22 [IQR, 136.90-194.66] vs. 108.00 [IQR, 100.46-125.88] pg/mL; p < 0.001), and IL-8 (66.83 [IQR, 57.70-82.82] vs. 43.62 [IQR, 32.89-50.59] pg/mL; p = 0.001) were higher after thoracotomy than after VATS; differences at 48 h persisted for TNF-α (2.48 [IQR, 1.86-3.04] vs. 1.99 [IQR, 1.19-2.23] pg/mL; p = 0.010) and IL-8 (16.92 [IQR, 15.09-23.99] vs. 7.42 [IQR, 6.44-11.30] pg/mL; p < 0.001). Pleural-fluid IL-6 at 24 h and IL-8 at 48 h were also higher after thoracotomy, whereas BAL cytokines did not differ significantly by approach. Longitudinal GEE analyses showed significant approach-by-time interactions for serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8 and for pleural-fluid IL-8, but not for pleural-fluid IL-6. Conclusions: VATS was associated with a lower systemic proinflammatory response than open thoracotomy, while differences in the pleural compartment were more limited and no detectable difference was observed in early alveolar cytokine responses. These findings highlight compartment-specific differences in perioperative inflammatory responses between VATS and open thoracotomy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the effects of varying doses of aerosolized Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) on oxygenation and intrapulmonary shunt fraction (Qs/Qt) during One-Lung Ventilation (OLV) under 60% Fraction of Inspired Oxygen (FiO2). Secondary objectives included evaluating the impact on intraoperative hypoxemia, postoperative Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS), and Postoperative Pulmonary Complications (PPCs). DESIGN: A prospective, single center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial. SETTING: The study was conducted at a single academic medical center. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 160 patients aged 65‒84 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III and Body Mass Index (BMI) < 30 kg/m2, undergoing elective esophageal cancer surgery were enrolled. Patients with certain comorbidities, respiratory diseases, or contraindications to PGE1 were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned to one of four groups: Group L ‒ Received 0.1 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group M ‒ Received 0.2 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group H ‒ Received 0.3 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group C (control) ‒ Received normal saline nebulization. Nebulization was performed for 10-minutes via a modified breathing circuit into the ventilated lung before initiating OLV. MEASUREMENTS: Arterial blood gas parameters (arterial partial pressure of oxygen, PaO2; arterial oxygen saturation, SaO2; arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide, PaCO2), hemodynamic variables (Mean Arterial Pressure [MAP]; Heart Rate [HR]), respiratory mechanics (Peak airway pressure [Ppeak]; dynamic lung compliance [Cdyn]), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and Qs/Qt were recorded at multiple time points during OLV. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia and hypotension, PPCs within 7-days, and CPIS on postoperative day-2 were also assessed. MAIN RESULTS: All PGE1 groups showed significantly improved PaO2, SaO2, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and reduced Qs/Qt during the first 30-minutes of OLV compared to the control group. The High-dose group (H) demonstrated the greatest improvement in oxygenation. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [Group L: 0/40 (0%), Group M: 0/40 (0%), Group H: 0/40 (0%), Group C: 3/40 (7.5%)] and hypotension did not differ significantly among groups; however, the hypoxemia finding was exploratory as the study was not powered for this endpoint. No significant differences were observed in PPCs incidence among groups, but group H was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 compared to group C. Hemodynamic changes were transient and clinically manageable. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulized PGE1 at doses of 0.1-0.3 μg/kg improves oxygenation and reduces Qs/Qt during OLV under 60% oxygen, with the 0.3 μg/kg dose being most effective. It did not significantly reduce the incidence of PPCs within 7-days. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was lower in the PGE1 groups (0/120) compared with the control group (3/40), but this was an exploratory finding as the study was not powered for this endpoint. The higher dose (0.3 μg/kg) was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 (3.3 vs. 4.1), but CPIS is a surrogate marker, and this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. The clinical significance of this small difference is uncertain, as changes of this magnitude are below the typically recognized thresholds for meaningful clinical improvement. Hemodynamic monitoring is recommended when using higher doses of PGE1.

papers.abstract_en: Trilaciclib, a cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 (CDK4/6) inhibitor administered before chemotherapy, reduces chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression (CIM) in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), but its efficacy across solid tumors remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of trilaciclib in solid tumor patients receiving chemotherapy. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to January 21, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing chemotherapy with or without trilaciclib were included. Primary outcomes were severe neutropenia (SN), febrile neutropenia (FN), duration of severe neutropenia (DSN), Grade 3/4 leukopenia, and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) use. Secondary outcomes included other hematologic toxicities, supportive care interventions, and efficacy outcomes. Ten studies involving 1172 patients (six RCTs and four cohort studies) were identified. Trilaciclib significantly reduced SN (OR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.06-0.31; p < 0.001), FN (OR, 0.19; 95% CI, 0.11-0.36; p < 0.001), Grade 3/4 leukopenia (OR, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.13-0.46; p < 0.001), and G-CSF use (OR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.18-0.71; p = 0.0087), and shortened DSN (MD, -2.30 days; 95% CI, -4.28 to -0.31; p = 0.0309). It also reduced Grade 3/4 anemia and thrombocytopenia and decreased use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, red blood cell transfusions, and platelet transfusions. Overall survival showed a borderline improvement (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.71-0.99; p = 0.0373), while no significant differences were observed in progression-free survival, overall response rate, or non-hematologic adverse events. Subgroup analyses suggested greater benefit in ES-SCLC. Overall, trilaciclib before chemotherapy significantly reduced CIM and supportive care needs, with no apparent compromise in antitumor efficacy and more pronounced effects in ES-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Esophageal leiomyoma is the most common benign mesenchymal tumor of the esophagus. Minimally invasive management is performed by thoracoscopic surgery or endoscopic resection, but comparative evidence remains limited. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes and treatment-selection patterns for thoracic and endoscopic resection. METHODS: Patients with pathologically confirmed leiomyoma who underwent resection between January 2015 and September 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients with malignant components, biopsy/fine-needle aspiration only, or incomplete data were excluded. A 1:1 propensity score matching analysis was performed using nearest-neighbor matching with a caliper of 0.1, matching age, sex, tumor location, and maximal tumor diameter. RESULTS: A total of 1,348 patients were included in the primary analysis: 132 underwent minimally invasive thoracic surgery and 1,216 underwent endoscopic resection. In the endoscopic group, 54.5% underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection and 45.5% underwent submucosal tunneling endoscopic resection. In the MIS group, 62 patients (47.0%) received intraoperative endoscopic assistance. Endoscopic resection was associated with shorter operative duration (41.9 ± 39.9 vs 114.8 ± 71.0 min, p < 0.001) and shorter postoperative hospital stay (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days, p < 0.001), whereas minimally invasive thoracic surgery was used for larger tumors (median 5.0 vs 1.3 cm, p < 0.001). After matching, 113 pairs were analyzed. Endoscopic resection remained associated with shorter operative duration (73.7 ± 62.9 vs 111.6 ± 61.5 min, p = 0.009) and shorter postoperative hospital stay (median 3.0 vs 5.0 days, p < 0.001). In the matched cohort, nasogastric tube placement and delayed stay of 5 days or longer were less common after endoscopic resection. CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic resection was associated with faster postoperative recovery in patients with esophageal leiomyoma, whereas thoracic surgery remained important for larger tumors and complex lesions. These findings support a size- and location-oriented treatment strategy rather than a universal preference for either approach.

Conclusions: Among carefully selected octogenarians undergoing robotic anatomic lung resection for NSCLC, no statistically significant differences in short-term postoperative outcomes were detected compared with patients aged 65-75 years after adjustment for baseline differences. These findings support individualized surgical selection beyond chronologic age alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Identification of metastasis status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a critical part of understanding disease prognosis, treatment courses, trial eligibility, and population-level cancer surveillance. However, metastasis status is inconsistently recorded in structured cancer registry fields, since manual abstraction of clinical notes is often an error-prone process. This challenge highlights an opportunity for leveraging large language models (LLMs) to conduct high-scale metastasis extraction from real-world clinical documentation. OBJECTIVE: We conducted a retrospective, multicohort comparative evaluation of 3 distinct LLMs for 2 independent classification tasks: overall metastasis presence at any site and brain/central nervous system (CNS) metastasis presence. We evaluated model performance on 2 independent NSCLC cohorts: one with registry labels and another with manual annotations. We further explored whether our methods could analyze clinical documentation and recover missing information in structured registry fields. METHODS: Patient cohorts were derived from the Winship Cancer Institute. Cohort 1 (n=579 patients; 24,887 notes across 69 note types; 2023-2025) used registry-linked metastasis fields as the reference standard. Cohort 2 (n=22 patients; 644 radiology notes; 2010-2021) was drawn from 2 completed randomized trials and used dual-annotated labels (Cohen κ: 0.93 overall metastasis; 0.88 CNS metastasis) as the reference standard. We fine-tuned the GatorTron-base encoder model for each independent binary classification task. We evaluated MedGemma-27B-text and Llama 3.1-70B using zero-shot prompting. A separate cohort of 675 patients with missing registry labels was used for an exploratory missingness-recovery analysis, validated against annotations of a random subsample. Our best-performing model was used to conduct further site-specific metastasis classification, based on available registry data. RESULTS: More than half (675/1260, 54%) of initially identified cohort 1 patients had missing or unknown registry metastasis labels. MedGemma demonstrated the best performance in overall metastasis classification (cohort 1: F1-score=0.80; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=1.0; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.93). For brain/CNS metastasis, Llama3 performed best in both cohorts (cohort 1: F1-score=0.79; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=0.93; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.86). The fine-tuned GatorTron model showed strong performance for classification of overall metastasis in cohort 1 (F1-score=0.72). Error analysis indicated that several model errors reflected incomplete registry labels, ambiguous clinical language, or missing documentation. In the exploratory recovery analysis, model predictions agreed with manual annotations at an accuracy of 0.90 and F1-score of 0.89. Additional site-specific metastasis classification by MedGemma demonstrated high performance for liver metastasis (F1-score=0.82) and bone metastasis (F1-score=0.79). CONCLUSIONS: All models demonstrated relatively high performance. The zero-shot generative models were more robust to nuanced documentation and context-dependent brain/CNS metastasis extraction. The fine-tuned encoder model demonstrated strong classification performance but may have been limited by potential inaccuracies in the registry reference standards during model training. This study further demonstrated the potential of LLMs in recovering plausible structured labels from narrative text, complementing cancer registries for metastasis ascertainment.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Chemoradioimmunotherapy (CRIT) with 60-66 Gy is the standard of care (SoC) for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) UICC stage III. The aim of this real-world data (RWD) study was to report the long-term impact of Durvalumab and radiation dose escalation on clinical outcomes. MATERIAL AND METHODS: ALLSTAR is a nationwide prospective multicentre registry for NSCLC UICC stage III, in which 12/14 Austrian centres participated (ethics approval number: 1002/2019). The basis for the current analysis is the third data extraction, which was completed on 2 June 2025. Apart from the SoC, alternative dose-fractionation and sequential CRT concepts >66 Gy were also permitted. Durvalumab maintenance treatment for one year was administered at the discretion of the tumour board at each centre. RESULTS: Compared to prior analyses by our group, 40 individuals who completed follow-up (FUP) were added to this final analysis, leading to a total patient population of 228 (156 CRT plus Durvalumab; 72 CRT). In 156 patients, Durvalumab was added to CRT, while 72 received CRT only. The median FUP periods were 41.0 (95%-CI: 36.7-45.4) and 37.8 months (95%-CI: 31.4-44.1) for the Durvalumab and CRT cohort, respectively. Radiation dose escalation combined with Durvalumab treatment was associated with a nominally higher ITC of 37 months (95%-CI: 24.5-not reached) compared with 17.7 months (95%-CI: 14.9-not reached) in patients receiving neither dose escalation nor Durvalumab (N = 135; HR = 0.61; 95%-CI: 0.37-1.006; p-value 0.051). With Durvalumab maintenance, a median PFS of 22.8 months (95%-CI: 19.4-38.3) was observed compared to 16.5 months (95%-CI: 12.6-24.5) without (N = 228; HR = 0.61; 95%-CI: 0.42-0.88; p-value 0.0071). Median OS was 52.6 months (95%-CI: 39.5-not reached) with Durvalumab compared to 27.4 months (95%-CI: 18.7-not reached) without (N = 228; HR = 0.52; 95%-CI: 0.34-0.78; log-rank p-value < 0.002). Median time to death or distant metastasis (TTDM) was 33.3 months (95%-CI: 23.5-45) in the Durvalumab cohort compared to 18.7 months (95%-CI: 14.8-not reached) in the CRT cohort (N = 228; HR = 0.60; 95%-CI: 0.42-0.89; log-rank p-value 0.01). Median time to death or local relapse (TDLR) with Durvalumab was 30.4 months (95%-CI: 23.5-51.1) compared to 17.2 months (95%-CI: 14.8-25.7) without (N = 226; HR = 0.58; 95%-CI: 0.40-0.83; log-rank p-value < 0.003). CONCLUSION: This final RWD analysis implies both a beneficial effect of high-dose irradiation combined with Durvalumab on ITC and the long-lasting impact of Durvalumab on PFS, OS, TTDM, and TDLR.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have become a standard treatment option for advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, considerable heterogeneity exists among patients regarding treatment response and survival. This study aimed to determine whether the pretreatment modified Glasgow Prognostic Score (mGPS), a marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, is prognostically associated with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC treated with nivolumab at a single tertiary oncology center. Methods: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 130 adult patients with histologically confirmed advanced/metastatic NSCLC who received nivolumab at the Department of Medical Oncology, Çukurova University Faculty of Medicine. The pretreatment mGPS (0, 1, or 2), derived from baseline serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin levels, was analyzed in relation to PFS and OS using the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression. The prognostic value of mGPS was tested in multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, histology, brain metastasis, liver metastasis, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR); the proportional hazards assumption was formally tested, and the incremental discriminative contribution of mGPS was assessed using bootstrap resampling. Results: Among 130 patients, 83.8% received nivolumab as second-line therapy. Pretreatment mGPS was 0, 1, and 2 in 40 (30.8%), 55 (42.3%), and 35 (26.9%) patients, respectively. Median OS was not reached, 9.7 months, and 3.0 months across mGPS 0, 1, and 2, respectively; corresponding median PFS values were 10.2, 4.8, and 3.0 months (log-rank p < 0.001 for both endpoints). After adjustment for age, sex, ECOG performance status, histology, brain metastasis, liver metastasis, and NLR, each one-point increase in mGPS remained associated with worse OS (adjusted HR 2.38; 95% CI 1.64-3.46; p < 0.001) and PFS (adjusted HR 1.81; 95% CI 1.32-2.48; p < 0.001), independent of the covariates included in the model. The proportional hazards assumption held for mGPS in both models. Addition of mGPS to the clinical-variables-only model was associated with higher model discrimination (Harrell's C-index: 0.676 to 0.737 for OS and 0.620 to 0.666 for PFS), a difference confirmed as statistically significant by bootstrap resampling (2000 iterations; 95% CI for the difference excluding zero, p < 0.001 for both endpoints). Conclusions: Pretreatment mGPS is a simple, readily available marker that shows a robust prognostic-rather than treatment-predictive-association with both OS and PFS in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC treated predominantly as second-line nivolumab monotherapy. Its addition to established clinical variables was associated with a statistically significant, though modest, improvement in prognostic discrimination. These findings require prospective, multicenter validation, including in first-line immunotherapy settings, before mGPS can be recommended for routine clinical risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: The CRP-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index is promoted both as a marker of postoperative morbidity and as a prognostic factor for survival. These claims are rarely tested together, thresholds usually come from the dataset in which they are then tested, and the index is seldom compared against its components. We examined both in one minimally invasive esophagectomy cohort. Methods: Consecutive esophagectomies with a thoracoscopic or robotic thoracic phase at one centre were reviewed. The index was derived from the preoperative albumin, C-reactive protein, and lymphocyte count. Short-term endpoints were major morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ 3) and anastomotic leak; survival was analysed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods, with internal cut-points stress-tested by bootstrapping. Results: Of 154 esophagectomies screened, 22 open or transhiatal procedures and one exploration without resection were excluded, leaving 131 patients. Major morbidity occurred in 39 (29.8%), and leak in 21 (16.0%). The index discriminated neither: area under the curve 0.556 (95% CI: 0.450-0.663) and 0.481 (95% CI: 0.339-0.623). Over a median follow-up of 31.0 months, there were 39 deaths, and median survival was 62.1 months. Here, the index behaved differently: each unit of log-CALLY carried a hazard ratio of 0.776 (95% CI: 0.643-0.936, p = 0.008), and three-year survival rose from 48.5% in the lowest tertile to 77.1% in the highest (trend p = 0.020). The association held after adjustment for stage and nodal status (0.749, 95% CI: 0.609-0.922, p = 0.006), lifting the concordance index of a stage-based model from 0.699 to 0.741. However, entered with CRP, the index lost significance. Conclusions: The index said nothing useful about early surgical morbidity yet was independently associated with survival, although that signal did not survive adjustment for CRP alone. It belongs with prognostic markers rather than perioperative risk scores.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Surgical resection remains an important treatment option for selected patients with bronchiectasis who have persistent symptoms, recurrent pulmonary infections, or hemoptysis despite medical therapy. This study evaluated perioperative and follow-up outcomes after pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis in a predominantly video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)-treated cohort. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients who underwent pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis between January 2009 and January 2026. Baseline and follow-up data were analyzed at the patient level, whereas operative and perioperative outcomes were assessed at the procedure level. Follow-up duration was calculated from the most recent resection to the last available clinical assessment. Results: Thirty-four patients underwent 37 pulmonary resections. Multilobar disease was present in 14 procedures (37.8%). VATS was used in 30 procedures (81.1%) and thoracotomy in 7 (18.9%). Median hospital stay was 11 days (range, 4-41). Postoperative complications occurred after 6 procedures (16.2%), with no 30-day mortality. Complete or partial symptomatic improvement occurred after 31 procedures (83.8%). Median follow-up was 20.8 months (interquartile range, 5.9-58.8; range, 0.4-144.2). At the last available clinical assessment, 23 patients (67.6%) had no recorded symptoms; recurrent hemoptysis occurred in 1 (2.9%) and recurrent pulmonary infection in 2 (5.9%). Conclusions: Pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis was associated with acceptable morbidity, no 30-day mortality, and a high rate of postoperative clinical improvement in this VATS-dominant cohort. Most patients had no recorded symptoms at their last available clinical assessment, while recurrent hemoptysis and pulmonary infection were uncommon.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The necessity of routine pulmonary parenchymal wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations (CLMs) in children remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association of routine wound closure with drainage-related recovery, perioperative outcomes, one-year computed tomography (CT)-based lung re-expansion, and the procedural learning curve. METHODS: Consecutive children who underwent thoracoscopic sublobar resection for CLMs between January 2021 and March 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. The cohort was divided into a non-closure group and a routine-closure group according to wound management strategy. Pulmonary wound closure was performed using an absorbable barbed suture, generally proceeding from the peripheral or lower-tension side toward the central or higher-tension region. Irregular wounds were managed by initiating closure from multiple peripheral points converging centrally while preserving the natural axis of residual bronchi and vasculature. Outcomes included chest tube duration, drainage volume, prolonged air leak, chest tube reinsertion, postoperative hospital stay, perioperative complications, one-year CT-based volumetric indices, and closure-time learning curve metrics. RESULTS: A total of 285 children were included, comprising 75 in the non-closure group and 210 in the closure group. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Compared with the non-closure group, the closure group exhibited significantly shorter chest tube duration (0.87 ± 0.74 vs. 2.81 ± 1.99 days, P < 0.001), lower postoperative drainage volume (2.12 ± 0.70 vs. 7.21 ± 2.58 mL/kg/day, P < 0.001), reduced rates of prolonged air leak and drainage failure, and shorter postoperative hospital stay (5.63 ± 0.83 vs. 7.68 ± 2.10 days, P < 0.001). At one-year follow-up, CT-based volumetric assessment revealed no evidence that wound closure restricted residual lung re-expansion. Closure time decreased from approximately 22 min in the early phase to 11 min in the late phase, with learning curve inflection points identified at cases 47 and 135. CONCLUSIONS: Routine pulmonary wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for pediatric CLMs was associated with improved drainage-related recovery and shorter hospitalization, without compromising one-year lung re-expansion on CT. Although closure adds a procedural step, efficiency improved substantially with experience, demonstrating a quantifiable learning curve.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Therapeutic strategies after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) remain suboptimal in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We investigated whether continuing EGFR inhibition with lazertinib combined with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy could extend clinical benefit after progression on prior lazertinib. METHODS: In the multicenter, single-arm, phase II LUCAS study (NCT05786430), patients with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC who had progressed on lazertinib received lazertinib 240 mg daily plus pemetrexed-carboplatin for four cycles, followed by maintenance lazertinib and pemetrexed. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), intracranial PFS, safety, and exploratory ctDNA analyses. RESULTS: Of 86 patients, 46.5% had a history of brain metastases. Among 81 response-evaluable patients, median PFS was 9.5 months (95% CI: 6.3-9.6; one-sided p = 0.017 against a null median of 6.0 months). In the safety population, median OS was 15.9 months (95% CI: 12.4-20.0) and ORR was 36.0% (95% CI: 26.0-47.1). Outcomes were similar irrespective of prior lazertinib line or EGFR subtype. Baseline ctDNA-detected EGFR amplification was associated with inferior survival. Among 36 patients with radiologically evident baseline brain metastases, median intracranial PFS was 9.9 months (95% CI: 7.8-16.4) with infrequent isolated intracranial progression. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events occurred in 69.8%, predominantly hematologic, without new safety signals. CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of lazertinib with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy after progression on prior lazertinib was associated with meaningful systemic and intracranial activity and manageable toxicity. Randomized evaluation is required to establish the incremental benefit of lazertinib continuation.

papers.abstract_en: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (NIVATS) minimises airway trauma and ventilator-induced lung injury, yet its application in complex, multi-phase McKeown oesophagectomy is seldom reported. A 32-year-old female (40 kg, 140 cm and body mass index: 20.4 kg/m 2 ) presented for McKeown minimally invasive oesophagectomy following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. We employed a 'less invasive anaesthesia' strategy combining T9-T10 thoracic epidural analgesia with Bispectral Index-guided target-controlled propofol infusion. Continuous pressure support ventilation (16 cmH 2 O above a positive end-expiratory pressure of 5 cmH 2 O) with preserved spontaneous breathing was maintained via a size 3 i-gel™ throughout surgery; neuromuscular blockade and controlled mechanical ventilation were not used at any stage. Surgical exposure was optimised via right-sided capnothorax. The resulting permissive hypercapnia was haemodynamically well-tolerated. Recovery was uneventful, and the airway device was removed after protective airway reflexes had returned. She was discharged from the hospital on post-operative day 6 without any complications. NIVATS for McKeown oesophagectomy may be feasible in carefully selected patients.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning model to improve postoperative risk stratification and predict adjuvant therapy benefit in stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and Methods In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with stage I NSCLC, a multimodal model called the Deep Learning-Radiomic-Text Transformer (DLRTransformer) was developed by integrating multiview 2.5-dimensional deep learning features from CT scans, radiomics, clinical variables, and prognostic embeddings extracted from pathology reports using a large language model. A central transformer architecture fuses these features to predict disease-free survival. Model performance was evaluated on independent external datasets and compared with guideline-based risk stratification. Associations between model-derived risk scores and tumor microenvironment features were analyzed to assess biologic interpretability. Results A total of 1073 patients (mean age ± SD, 60.8 years ± 9.8; 550 male) were enrolled from five centers. On external datasets, DLRTransformer demonstrated robust prognostic performance (concordance index, 0.77-0.78), outperforming the guideline-based risk stratification (concordance index, 0.60-0.65). Risk scores were associated with tumor microenvironment phenotypes, including increased neoplastic cellularity and reduced tertiary lymphoid structures. A treatment-by-risk interaction was observed (interaction hazard ratio [HR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.32; P < .01). In propensity score-matched subcohorts, adjuvant therapy improved disease-free survival in high-risk patients (HR, 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.84; P = .02) but not in low-risk patients (HR, 1.70; 95% CI: 0.97, 2.99; P = .06). Conclusion The DLRTransformer improved postoperative risk stratification compared with guideline-based risk stratification and identified patients with stage I NSCLC who benefited from adjuvant therapy. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Precise localization is critical for sublobar resection of small pulmonary nodules. We evaluated the safety, technical efficiency, and clinical outcomes of preoperative percutaneous dye-localization using a cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-enabled flat-panel detector interventional fluoroscopy system in a hybrid operating room (HOR). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 74 consecutive patients (137 lesions) who underwent image-guided localization followed by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) sublobar resection (wedge resection or segmentectomy) between 2022 and 2023 at Chia-Yi Christian Hospital. Procedural workflow, localization success, surgical margins, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. RESULTS: Technical localization success was achieved in 100% of lesions (mean nodule diameter: 8.59 ± 4.85 mm). The procedure required a mean of 1.31 ± 0.67 puncture attempts per lesion at a mean depth of 5.22 ± 1.86 cm. Procedure-related pneumothorax occurred in 29.7% (22/74) of patients, with 14.9% (11/74) requiring pigtail catheter drainage; pneumothorax occurrence was significantly associated with multiple puncture attempts (p < 0.001) and lower-lobe lesions (p = 0.001). Lower-lobe location was significantly associated with requiring more puncture attempts (p = 0.028). For malignant lesions, the mean pathological resection margin was 17.16 ± 8.73 mm, with 92.31% achieving a margin-to-tumor ratio (MTR) ≥ 1. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 3.04 ± 1.16 days. CONCLUSIONS: Single-stage image-guided dye-localization and VATS sublobar lung resection in an HOR using a biplane CBCT-enabled platform is safe, feasible, and effective. This streamlined workflow ensures high technical success and adequate surgical margins with manageable complications. Further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term oncological outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet predicting durable benefit and detecting resistance remain major challenges. As immunotherapy expands across disease stages, minimally invasive tools are increasingly needed to monitor response and inform treatment personalization. Liquid biopsy enables serial assessment of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and other blood-based biomarkers, complementing tissue analysis and imaging. This review critically synthesizes evidence across resectable, locally advanced, and metastatic NSCLC, integrating ctDNA dynamics with emerging multi-omics approaches. Its contribution is to distinguish the prognostic value of circulating biomarkers from evidence that using them to guide treatment improves patient outcomes, while identifying priorities for clinical translation. Across the reviewed studies, ctDNA clearance is associated with favorable outcomes, whereas persistent or rising ctDNA signals an increased risk of recurrence or progression, sometimes before radiological detection. Methylation, fragmentomics, plasma proteomics, and immune-cell profiling may provide complementary information on tumor-immune interactions. However, low tumor shedding, clonal hematopoiesis, assay variability, and unvalidated intervention thresholds limit routine use. The expansion of perioperative immunotherapy and emerging interest in biomarker-guided treatment adaptation make this synthesis timely. Prospective interventional trials are needed to determine whether liquid biopsy can safely guide treatment escalation, de-escalation, or discontinuation. By clarifying both the promise and the limitations of longitudinal monitoring, this review informs research aimed at detecting ineffective treatment earlier and reducing unnecessary treatment exposure while preserving cancer control.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Chronobiology may influence outcomes in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but its prognostic role in early-stage disease remains unclear. Chronobiological and inflammatory variables included season of surgery (spring/summer [21st March-22nd September], autumn/winter [23rd September-20th March]), time of day, day of week, and preoperative (CRP0 levels: low ≤ 3 mg/L, high > 3 mg/L) and postoperative day-3 (CRP3 levels: low ≤ 126 mg/L, high > 126 mg/L) C-reactive protein levels. The cohort was randomly divided into training (70%) and testing (30%) sets to develop and validate a prognostic model for overall survival (OS), taking into consideration the follow-up time. Disease-free survival (DFS) was analyzed as a secondary endpoint. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 6.7 years, with 80 deaths and 108 recurrences recorded. In the training set, older age (p = 0.0049), stage IB disease (p = 0.0301), high CRP0 (p = 0.0049), and high CRP3 (p = 0.0280) were associated with worse OS, while surgery performed during autumn/winter was associated with improved OS (p = 0.0312). The resulting linear predictor remained associated with both OS and DFS in the overall population. CONCLUSIONS: A simple model integrating age, pathological stage, and season of surgery was associated with long-term outcomes after surgery in stage I NSCLC. This model provides an exploratory framework integrating host-, tumor-, and chronobiological dimensions of prognosis. These findings require external validation and further investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying seasonal variation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy defined by rapid progression, early metastasis, and profound therapeutic resistance. Its extensive heterogeneity across genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and microenvironmental levels continues to undermine precision medicine. Emerging evidence highlights the complex role of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) alterations, histologic transformation from EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to SCLC, and the influence of distinct transcriptional subtypes on clinical behavior. After multivariable logistic regression, cirrhosis was associated with higher mortality odds at 30 days (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.39-3.99, p < 0.001) and 90 days (OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.38-3.21, p < 0.001); higher 90-day post-operative complications odds (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14-1.81, p = 0.002); and higher hospital readmission odds at 30 days (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.41-2.56, p < 0.001) and 90 days (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.27-2.10, p = 0.001). However, when liver-related mortality was a competing event, association between cirrhosis and cancer-specific mortality was absent (sHR 1.04, 95% CI 0.95-1.13, p = 0.395). A lower proportion of patients with cirrhosis received systemic treatments (31% versus 40%, p < 0.001), and a greater proportion experienced post-treatment complications: electrolyte disturbances (10% versus 5%, p < 0.001), kidney injury (5% versus 2%, p = 0.012), and thrombocytopenia (7% versus 2%, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhosis is associated with increased morbidity and mortality in stage 1-3 NSCLC patients undergoing curative surgery. Stage 4 NSCLC patients with cirrhosis are less likely to receive palliative treatment and may experience more post-treatment complications.

papers.abstract_en: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness and fatigability. Perioperative management is challenging because patients may have bulbar or respiratory muscle involvement and altered sensitivity to neuromuscular blocking agents, increasing the risk of postoperative respiratory failure and myasthenic crisis. Thymectomy is an established therapeutic option in selected patients with myasthenia gravis and may be performed using minimally invasive thoracoscopic techniques. We report the anesthetic management of a 48-year-old man with generalized acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MGFA class IIb) scheduled for thoracoscopic thymectomy. The patient had a recent relapse with diplopia, dysphagia, and easy fatigability, which improved after medical therapy. Preoperative optimization included intravenous immunoglobulin therapy for four days. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and remifentanil without initial neuromuscular blockade. Tracheal intubation was facilitated using video laryngoscopy after topical lidocaine. Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane, and invasive monitoring was established. Because of the surgical requirement for improved thoracoscopic visualization, a reduced dose of rocuronium was administered intraoperatively under train-of-four monitoring. At the end of surgery, neuromuscular blockade was reversed with sugammadex, and the patient was successfully extubated and transferred to the intensive care unit in stable condition. This case highlights the importance of careful preoperative optimization, avoidance of neuromuscular blocking agents when possible, quantitative neuromuscular monitoring, and individualized use of low-dose rocuronium with sugammadex reversal when muscle relaxation is required during thoracoscopic thymectomy in patients with myasthenia gravis.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and resistance to targeted therapy and immunotherapy represents a substantial unmet clinical need. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as a promising therapeutic class. AREAS COVERED: This drug evaluation summarizes the pharmacological rationale, molecular design, preclinical activity, clinical efficacy, safety profile, and regulatory development of sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT; MK-2870/SKB264) in NSCLC. Relevant evidence was identified through searches of PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, major oncology congress proceedings, and regulatory announcements through 20 September 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Randomized trials have demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) with sac-TMT versus docetaxel and platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated advanced NSCLC after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) progression. In advanced NSCLC without actionable driver alterations, sac-TMT plus pembrolizumab improved PFS versus pembrolizumab alone in programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-positive disease; however, overall survival (OS) remains immature, and superiority over contemporary chemoimmunotherapy has not been established. The principal clinically relevant toxicities are hematologic toxicity and stomatitis. Future studies should clarify predictive biomarkers, optimal treatment sequencing, intracranial activity, and generalizability, while generating mature survival and quality-of-life data.

papers.abstract_en: In a cancer clinical trial with an immunotherapy, the treatment often becomes effective after a certain delay time. It is well known that traditional log-rank test no longer provides optimal power in this case. There has been a great interest to search for a more powerful test to detect a truly effective immunotherapy treatment. In this paper, we propose a new testing method based on the maximum value of a set of 0-1 weighted log-rank test statistics and establish useful theoretical results of the relevant test statistics. Extensive simulation studies are conducted to examine the empirical performance of the proposed method. An analysis of the real data from a non-small-cell lung cancer clinical trial is also carried out to further demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed test method. papers.abstract_en: Perioperative treatment plays an increasingly important role in improving outcomes for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) offers a new perspective for optimizing individualized perioperative management. This review systematically examines the core value of ctDNA in perioperative therapy for resectable NSCLC, encompassing its correlation with treatment response and pathological remission during the neoadjuvant phase, its utility as a dynamic monitor of treatment efficacy, and its emerging role in prognostic stratification and recurrence prediction in the postoperative setting. Importantly, while ctDNA demonstrates considerable promise for guiding individualized perioperative management, most applications remain investigational; we therefore distinguish between established correlative uses and prospective strategies currently under evaluation in clinical trials. It also addresses current technical challenges in ctDNA application, including limited sensitivity, false positives, lack of standardization, cost-effectiveness concerns, and difficulties in integration into clinical decision-making. Future prospective interventional studies are needed to validate ctDNA-guided treatment adjustments and to establish standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration pathways, thereby facilitating the integration of ctDNA into the full course of perioperative management for NSCLC and enabling precise efficacy assessment, risk stratification, and individualized treatment decisions.
